default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t106-p1.vietnamese:
In Japan, it is customary to exchange business cards (Note 1) when meeting someone for the first time in a business setting. However, countries that use business cards, such as South Korea and Japan, seem to be very rare ( A ). In some countries, business cards are hardly used at all; in others, only certain special people use them. There are also countries where only people who work with foreign countries have business cards. In addition, some people do things that Japanese people would absolutely never do, such as writing a note on a business card they have just received right in front of the other person. However, since etiquette differs from country to country, we should not get angry just because it differs from Japanese customs.

Rules of politeness when exchanging business cards

1. Hold out the business card with both hands, saying the company name and your own name, with the card oriented so that the recipient can read it.

2. The person of lower status presents their card first to the person of higher status. Normally, an older person or someone with a higher position in the company is considered senior, but someone from a client company holds the higher position.

3. When several people present their cards at the same time, the highest-ranking person among the presenters gives their card first to the highest-ranking person on the receiving side.

4. When giving and receiving cards at the same time, use your right hand to give your card and your left hand to receive the other person's card. The person of lower status must hold out their card so that it is lower than the card of the person of higher status.

5. When receiving a card, be careful not to hold it in places such as the part where the name is printed.

6. After receiving a business card, do not put it away immediately. Leave it on the table ( B ) while talking.

(Note 1) Business card: a small piece of paper showing a person's name, company name, telephone number, and so on

(Note 2) Exchange: give something and receive something in return.

Since around 2000, an increasing number of people have believed that it is good for their children to have names that are different from everyone else’s. Rare, unusual, and gender-neutral names have increased considerably. Today, as many as 1 in 3 children has an unusual name, making things very difficult for teachers at school because they cannot read the names. Although the kanji that may be used in names are regulated, some people read kanji however they like, giving rise to “sparkly names” (Kirakira-names). Some children have names such as 「姫星」(Himeboshi/Kiti), 「光宙」(Pikachuu), and 「美月」(Mitsuki). As a result, among children with unusual names, some do not want to say their names, some feel embarrassed by them, and some always use a different name. These children are troubled by having been given such unusual names. In a survey about unusual names, 23.8% approved of them, while as many as 76.2% opposed them. Nevertheless, parents who put their feelings into such names and end up choosing them have not decreased. In the past, all of Japan was thrown into an uproar over the name “Akuma” (Devil). Someone intended to name their child Devil. At the time, many people objected, saying, “It would be terrible for the child to be named Devil.” In the end, the government did not approve the name “Akuma,” but people generally believe that names like this should not be given. Since a name is used more often by other people than by the person who has it, names that cannot be read can hardly be considered good. default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t11-p1.outline.2.n: While Katie is confused, Ms. Yamada notices her and starts talking to her, then leads Katie all the way to the boarding location.
default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t11-p1.outline.3.n: Yamada says that although he is on his way back to Kyoto, he is willing to take a later train to help because many kind people helped him while he was abroad. Katie thanks Yamada.
default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t11-p1.outline.4.n: While boarding the train, Katie recalls Yamada’s words, feels warmed by them, and wants to follow Yamada’s example of always helping people in difficulty.
default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t11-p1.vietnamese:
This is an essay written by Katie.

The Person I Met at Tokyo Station

Katie Wang

Last week, I went to visit a friend at her home. On the way there, I had to transfer trains at Tokyo Station, but because the station was so large, I did not know where I was supposed to transfer. So I walked back and forth through the station holding a note.

As I was anxiously thinking, “What should I do?”, a woman named Yamada spoke to me. Ms. Yamada had apparently seen me repeatedly walking back and forth while drinking tea at a café inside the station. When she asked, “Is something wrong?”, I replied, “I do not know where to go to catch my train.” Ms. Yamada accompanied me all the way to the platform for the train I was going to take.

Ms. Yamada said that she had come to Tokyo for work and was now preparing to return to Kyoto. I asked, “Do you have enough time?” Ms. Yamada said, “There are many Shinkansen trains to Kyoto, so it is fine if I take the next one. When I lived abroad, many people were kind to me too.” I said, “Thank you very much. I truly appreciate it.”

After boarding the train and being alone again, I remembered Ms. Yamada’s words and felt warm inside. Then I thought that I, too, wanted to be kind to people in difficulty, just as Ms. Yamada had been.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t110-p1.vietnamese:
The Shibuya Crossing in Tokyo is very famous, and many tourists come to take pictures and try crossing it. A scramble crossing is an intersection where all vehicles stop at the same time, allowing pedestrians to walk in any direction they wish. There are about 300 such crossings in Japan, but apparently none has as many people crossing at once as Shibuya. At the busiest times, about 3,000 people cross during the seven seconds that the traffic light is green, yet everyone moves skillfully. Tourists often come to watch because they find it fascinating. Even on rainy days, the scene is said to be beautiful as brightly colored umbrellas move across the intersection. Perhaps there is nowhere else quite like it.

December 31 is called New Year’s Eve (Omisoka), and on that night, as well as during Halloween and when World Cup soccer matches are being held, many young people gather there. Although no special event is organized, people seem to come because it looks exciting. Some drink alcohol, while others shout loudly. The police warn them, “Because it is dangerous, please do not gather near the crossing,” but they still refuse to leave. In a large crowd, no one knows what might happen. The crossing is even more dangerous because vehicles also pass through it. For this reason, the police are always worried that an accident will occur. Therefore, on New Year’s Eve in 2016, it was decided that vehicles would not be allowed to pass through the intersection. As a result, no traffic accident occurred, but apparently many people still caused trouble as usual.

Because water is made of hydrogen (Note 1) and oxygen (Note 2), it can be produced from air. However, in the past, almost no one thought about whether a machine like that was really necessary or whether water could actually be made from air. Today, machines can produce water from air in our homes, but these machines cannot produce much water, and the cost of producing it is very high.

However, a machine made in 2018 can produce 2,000 liters of water a day at a cost of only about 2 cents per liter. This is because the machine is powered by burning wood and other materials, so it does not require electricity. Although problems remain, such as the high price of the machine, it will surely be useful because many people are suffering from water shortages. Even so, we must not forget that the amount of water produced by this machine is only enough for drinking; it still cannot produce enough water to grow rice or vegetables.

As the population increases, water shortages are becoming more serious. There is a great deal of water on Earth (Note 4), but 97% of it is seawater, so it cannot be used as it is. The water in glaciers (Note 5) and groundwater among the remaining 3% is also difficult to use. The water that people can readily use amounts to only about 0.01% of the water in rivers and lakes.

It is said that as many as 663 million people (Note 6) worldwide do not have clean drinking water, and 300,000 children die each year from contaminated water. Japanese people apparently use as much as 300 liters of water a day, but I think that, no matter how abundant water may seem, we are using far too much of it wastefully. Japan may even suffer from water shortages someday. I think we must value and conserve water more.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t112-p1.vietnamese:
Japan has 16 national holidays (Note 1), more than many other countries. However, because few people use their annual paid leave (Note 2), the total number of days off per year is quite low compared with European countries, where some people take as much as a month off. As a result, some people worry: “If people do not rest, new ideas will not emerge, and if things remain as they are, Japan will have no future.” It is also said: “Taking time off work is not pointless. New ideas emerge while we rest.” For this reason, rest will become even more necessary from now on.

The government also wants people to rest more, so it has taken measures such as increasing the number of national holidays and designating the following Monday as a substitute holiday when a national holiday falls on a Sunday. In addition, four holidays that had traditionally been set on specific dates have been moved to the second or third Monday of the month. In this way, the government has deliberately tried to increase the number of opportunities for consecutive days off. As a result, travel agencies and hotels are delighted when the number of travelers increases. However, because the number of Mondays off has increased, schools lose many Monday class periods over the course of a year. In addition, when hospitals are closed from Saturday afternoon until Tuesday morning, anyone who becomes ill or injured during that period is forced to go to an emergency hospital (Note 4). On holidays, even emergency hospitals have fewer doctors, so there are cases in which patients cannot receive timely treatment.

When it comes to rest, which is fundamentally an individual matter, there is very little the government can do. To make it easier for people to rest, companies, workers, and society as a whole need to change. For that purpose, I think we should communicate more widely that rest is extremely important.

（Note 1）National holiday: A day off designated by the government to commemorate or celebrate an event.

（Note 2）Annual paid leave: Leave that employers are required by law to provide to workers.

（Note 3）Wasteful / pointless: Of no use.

（Note 4）Emergency hospital: A hospital that is open when ordinary hospitals are closed.

（☆）Work-style reform: Since 2019, the government has been promoting “Work-style reform (changes intended to improve the way people work).”

Its meaning is 「Good things will come to a home that is always filled with laughter」. Since people’s thoughts are not so different from one another, other countries probably have similar proverbs, even if they are phrased differently.

When we laugh, the condition of our bodies improves. This is because our immune system is strengthened and we are able to relax. Therefore, in everyday life, it is very beneficial to have an enjoyable conversation with someone or watch entertaining television programs. However, there are also times when we feel sad or distressed. It is said that even at such times, making a smiling face improves our mood in the same way. When researchers examined whether men or women laugh out loud more often, they found that 40% of men and 60% of women do so. Therefore, perhaps this is why women live longer. Children also laugh frequently, but people seem to laugh less as they get older. This is probably caused by pressure and stress. The more we laugh, the more likely we are to live a healthy and cheerful life. Laughter costs nothing. I do not think there is any method as effective as this.

Japan's population is declining, and there is a shortage of workers. Some people argue that the situation would improve if more elderly people and women worked. However, because of problems such as unsuitable working conditions and a lack of the childcare facilities needed by people with young children, some people who want to work are unable to do so. Japan today is not an easy society in which to work.

At present, the people working in place of Japanese workers are foreigners. Some are married to Japanese people or are descendants of people of Japanese origin, but most are international students and technical intern trainees. International students who are permitted to work 28 hours a week often work as cleaners, convenience-store clerks, workers in boxed-meal factories, or employees at izakaya. Most technical intern trainees work in fields such as agriculture, fishing, and manufacturing. Although technical intern trainees come to learn skills, they are instead forced to work for extremely low wages. Many have to borrow money to come to Japan, and because they cannot change jobs, they are unable to quit even when working conditions are terrible. Some have become ill, been injured, or even died. This problem must be addressed quickly. This is both for their sake and for our own, because if some people work under terrible conditions, the working conditions of others cannot improve either.

In 2018, a law was enacted allowing more foreigners to work in Japan. It is said that half of the technical intern trainees will switch to working under this law. Will this lead more foreigners to come and work in Japan? If Japan remains as difficult a country in which to work as it is now, foreigners will probably not choose Japan.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t119-p1.vietnamese:
Japan has many 「shinise」 (long-established businesses). 「Shinise」 are shops or companies that have operated and remained in business for many years. According to some statistics, 5,586 businesses (Note 1) worldwide have existed for more than 200 years, and reportedly more than half of them—3,146 businesses—are Japanese. Germany has 837, the Netherlands 222, and France 196. The world's oldest business is also said to have been founded in Japan in 578. In Japan, there appear to be 7 businesses over 1,000 years old, 32 over 500 years old, 3,146 over 200 years old, and as many as 50,000 over 100 years old. However, 89.4% of these businesses have fewer than even 300 employees. The apparent reasons why there are so many such businesses are: ① wars have rarely occurred in Japan, ② businesses have always valued their core business (Note 2), and ③ businesses have a long-term outlook (Note 3). All of these reasons are self-evident. In particular, when we consider how many companies during the economic bubble period (Note 4) neglected their core businesses and instead bought and sold land and houses, only to close down or fall into difficulty, we can clearly understand the importance of core business.

Valuing a core business does not mean continuing to do exactly the same thing forever. Businesses survive by continually improving their core operations to suit each period. GE, founded by Edison in 1892, still exists today because it changed in response to the times. Only businesses that both value their core business and continually take on new challenges (Note 5) can survive for more than 100 years. Once they stop taking on challenges, any long-established business will certainly come to an end at that moment.

(Note 1) Business: Here, this refers to a shop or company.

(Note 2) Core business: The main business.

(Note 3) Long-term outlook: Thinking about matters over a long period.

(Note 4) Bubble period: The period of rapid economic growth from late 1986 to early 1991.

(Note 5) Challenge: Trying to do something despite its difficulty.

Among the positions of director, department head, section chief, and manager, the director is the highest, followed by the department head, then the section chief, and finally the manager.

It is very important to know which seats are considered good. In a room, a seat near the tokonoma, the alcove where flowers are displayed, or a seat far from the entrance is considered better. A good seat is called the kamiza (the seat of honor).

In a taxi, the best seat is directly behind the driver, followed by the rear seat on the opposite left side, then the middle seat, and finally the seat next to the driver, which is called the passenger seat. However, because the middle seat in the back may be uncomfortable, I think it is a good idea to ask whether it would be all right to sit in the front passenger seat.

Also, in Japan, the person of higher status is usually allowed to enter the car first. Some people, such as elderly passengers, may find it tiring to go all the way to the seat behind the driver. It is best to ask them what they would prefer. In addition, when it is not a taxi but a car driven by a person of higher status, the passenger seat is the seat of honor, so be careful.

Look at the instructions for making 「Simple Tofu Dish」on the next page and answer the questions below. For each answer, choose the best answer from 1, 2, 3, and 4.

Simple Tofu Dish

Ingredients

Mixed ground meat (Note 1): 150 g

If unavailable, use ground beef or pork

Onion: half of a medium-sized onion

Ketchup: 5 tablespoons

Sauce: 5 tablespoons

Salt: a little

Pepper: a little

Tofu: 1 block

Melting cheese (Note 2): 100–150 g

Grated cheese: a little, if available

① Cut the tofu into cubes measuring approximately 1.5 cm × 1.5 cm × 1.5 cm and blanch it first (Note 3). If you do not blanch it first, it will take much longer later.

② Finely chop the onion (Note 4).

③ Put the onion, meat, ketchup, and sauce in a frying pan and cook for about 3–4 minutes (Note 5).

④ When step ③ is complete, add the salt and pepper, mix well (Note 6), and turn off the heat. The meat sauce is now ready. You can also use commercially available meat sauce.

⑤ Place the tofu in a heatproof dish (Note 7), cover it with the meat sauce, and place the melting cheese on top.

⑥ Finally, sprinkling grated cheese on top will make it even more delicious.

⑦ Heat it in an oven or microwave until the cheese melts. It will taste better if the cheese is browned in an oven.

※ Using eggplant instead of tofu is also delicious. I think you should try making it in several different ways.

（Note 1）Mixed ground meat: Beef and pork finely ground and mixed together. If stores do not sell it, you can mince the meat yourself.

（Note 2）Melting cheese: A type of cheese that softens when exposed to high temperatures.

（Note 3）Blanch: To heat something in boiling water without adding seasoning.

（Note 4）Finely chop: To cut something into very small pieces.

（Note 5）Cook/simmer: To put ingredients together with salt, sugar, and so on, add heat, and continue cooking until the ingredients become tender.

（Note 6）Mix/stir: To combine two or more things.

（Note 7）Heatproof: Able to withstand being heated by a flame or other heat source without being damaged.

When Satoko came home, this note was on the table.

Dear Satoko,

You’re home already. I’ve gone to your grandmother’s house. I’ll be back around 7:00.

This morning, Dad said, 「I’m out of cold medicine, so I’ll buy some and bring it home」, but there is still some medicine at home. If Dad calls, tell him he doesn’t need to buy any. I’ve already made dinner, so eat whenever you get hungry.

Love,
Mom

This is a direct-sales vegetable shop. It sells vegetables harvested in nearby areas. Some people here also introduce dishes made with those vegetables. My friend says they like this restaurant because they can choose from various kinds of curry rice, such as meat curry and vegetable curry. My hobby is taking photographs. Last week, I went to a famous location to photograph trains. The scenery was beautiful, and I could see trains running in a very cool-looking way. Both the mountains and the flowers were beautiful. However, there were so many people at the spot with a clear view of the trains that I could not take a good photograph. My mother often bakes sweets at home. She bakes the most in winter. She says that baking makes a freezing room warmer, and the smell of the sweets also warms her spirits. Another reason is that there are many ingredients to put into the batter. In particular, regarding fruit, Mother says: "If I think something will spoil unless we eat it quickly, I put it in a cake and bake it."

Mother rarely bakes in summer. Naturally, this is because it becomes too hot. She also does not bake at all when she is extremely busy with work, for example. She does not bake when she is feeling sad, either. At times like that, if I say, "I’m really craving your homemade sweets," Mother cheers up a little and sometimes bakes something for me.

When I eat the sweets Mother has made, I feel extremely happy and think: "Mom, I’m always grateful to you." Mother says: "When I get older and can no longer bake well, I won’t bake sweets anymore." But Mother herself loves sweets. I think that if she can no longer bake, I will ( ③ - bake for her ).

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t161-p1.vietnamese:
How many ballpoint pens does everyone have? In Japan, ballpoint pens first became known in 1947. Someone from an American pen manufacturer came to Japan and dropped many ballpoint pens from an airplane. The message was: “A pen this convenient has been created. Try using it and experience how wonderful it is.” They thought that if Japanese people understood how useful it was, ballpoint pens would sell well in Japan.

The Japanese people who picked up the pens carefully investigated how the ink flowed and began thinking about how to make similar pens. Within about two years, ballpoint pens could also be manufactured in Japan, and many people began using Japanese pens.

Dear Taichi,

Yesterday, I went to a friend’s house. On the way home, I was tired and accidentally fell asleep on the bus. When I woke up and looked outside, the bus had already reached the stop after the one where I wanted to get off. I hurried off that bus. Then I boarded a bus going in the opposite direction.

February 14 is Valentine’s Day. I had heard that in Japan, it is a day when women give chocolate to men they like. Since a new chocolate counter had opened at the shopping center, I went there on February 5. They had many kinds of chocolate on display, ranging from 100 yen to 5,000 yen. There was a type that looked delicious, but it cost as much as 2,000 yen, so I could not buy it. Instead, I bought the 500-yen type and went home.

When I went to work on February 14, Sachiko, a female employee, was giving chocolate to each of the men in the company. I asked, “Do you really like that many people?” Sachiko said, “This is called giri-choco, or courtesy chocolate. It is given to people who have helped you.” Then she gave some to me as well. Since I had thought Valentine’s chocolate meant (② chocolate given by women to men), I said, “I’m a woman, so I can’t accept this.” Sachiko replied, “This is tomo-choco, or friendship chocolate. It is given to friends.” I also heard that there is a type called gohōbi-choco, or reward chocolate, which people buy for themselves after working hard.

This is an essay written by Ekaterina.

The Store Manager at My Part-Time Job

Ekaterina Smirnov

I work part-time at a convenience store in Japan. People from many different countries work there together. Since I had never had a part-time job in my home country, it was very difficult at first. However, everyone was kind, so I soon became accustomed to the job. There was only one time when the store manager ever reprimanded me.

One day, when a customer buying cigarettes said, “Give me cigarette number 20,” I put on a serious expression, said loudly, “Yes, here are cigarettes number 20,” and handed them to him. The customer looked somewhat startled. After he left, the store manager told me, “Ekaterina, the way you speak is a little frightening. Try to speak more gently.” Apparently, I had been speaking too harshly. I think that because I was so focused on not making mistakes, I ended up sounding cold. The store manager advised me, “Just imagine that a family member or friend has come into the store.”

In addition, when she had free time, the store manager treated me to Japanese food and listened to me talk about many things. As a result, even though I could not see my family, I did not feel lonely. Whenever I had trouble, the store manager helped me like a mother. I think of the store manager as someone in my family （like a family member）.

Dear Mr./Ms. Sugisawa,

It is now October, and the weather has become quite cool. How are you?

It has been half a year since I graduated from the Japanese language school. I am currently studying at a vocational school in Osaka to prepare for a career in the hotel industry. Half of my class is Japanese, and the other half consists of people from various countries. Therefore, I can learn about many different cultures. My favorite class is practical training. During practical training, we practice serving food at tables and assisting customers. Yesterday, the students played the roles of customers and hotel employees and practiced together. That class was ① very enjoyable. Practicing is more fun than simply sitting in class and studying from a textbook.

In addition, I started working part-time at a hotel three months ago. The Osaka dialect is different from the Japanese I learned at school. For example, 「本当に」(really) is said as 「ほんまに」, and 「だめだ」(no good) is said as 「あかん」. Therefore, when I first started my part-time job, I had a very ② difficult time. Recently, I have finally begun to understand the Osaka dialect. Working part-time in addition to attending school is quite difficult, but the job is interesting, and I think it (will be useful for my future), so I am still doing my best.

Winter will be coming soon, and there will probably be snow where you live, which must be difficult. Please take very good care of yourself.

October 15, 2022

Nguyen Thi Hoa

This is a composition written by Kim.

What I Want to Work Hard at This Year

Kim Leixin

A new year has begun. Around this time, many people start exercising. December is the end of the year, so there are many parties and people eat a lot of delicious food. As a result, they may have eaten too much and gained weight. Therefore, after January begins, they start exercising to lose weight.

I also plan to exercise this year, but that is not why I am starting. Recently, I have been suffering from back pain. When I went to the hospital recently, the doctor told me that I sit too much and advised me to stand up and walk more.

Therefore, I decided to walk every day this year. Yesterday, after lunch, I also walked around the office for a while. Although my lower back still hurt, I felt that my body had become a little lighter. In the afternoon, I was able to work in a relaxed mood.

When I told a senior colleague about this, they showed me something very useful. Apparently, they had also suffered from back pain for a while, but it improved after they started swimming. They also said that they felt very happy as they gradually became able to swim for longer periods. (I am a very poor swimmer.) However, since they recommended a good swimming class to me, I would like to give it a try this year.

This is a composition written by Emma.

Part-Time Work

Oneto Emma

I came to Japan last April. Life is difficult, but very enjoyable. I currently work part-time at a nursing home where 20 elderly people live. A senior student who lives in the same dormitory introduced me to the job. That senior also introduced me to better-paying part-time jobs at restaurants and hotels, but I immediately chose this one. That is because in the future, I want to work in a job that supports the lives of elderly people.

At first, I cleaned the hallways and restrooms. After doing that for two weeks, I spent a month cleaning each resident’s room. Now I also help the residents eat and go for walks.

Recently, I asked Mr. Ishida, a full-time employee, why I had initially been assigned only cleaning duties. Mr. Ishida said:「It was so that everyone could get to know you. If someone they did not know suddenly appeared and they were told, 『Starting today, this person will help you with your meals and walks,』 they might feel uncomfortable. When they see you cleaning, greet one another, and come to understand what kind of person you are, they can feel at ease.」I understood the reason very well.

I have now become close to the residents and enjoy my work very much. This part-time job has made my desire to「do this kind of work」in the future even stronger.

This is an essay written by You.

Computers and Smartphones

You Shunkou

The first time I touched a computer was in 1990. That was when I graduated from university and started working for a company. I still remember how difficult it was because I could not remember how to use it. However, I once thought that young people nowadays were all born with computers and could certainly use them easily.

However, this seems to be somewhat different. There is a new university graduate working at my company who is not good with computers. When I asked why, he replied that he had not used them much. He said that he had only touched computers a little during classes in high school and had hardly used them at university. Furthermore, he said that when writing reports for homework, he always used a smartphone, so he had no difficulty writing them. I was extremely surprised to hear this.

Perhaps someday there will be an era when people do all their work at companies using only smartphones or tablets. However, (at companies today, being able to use a computer is extremely important). Therefore, for people who want to work at a company, I hope they will learn how to use a computer before joining one.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t19-p1.vietnamese:
The word 「sumimasen」 appears frequently in Japanese conversation. For example, if a train suddenly jolts and someone accidentally steps on the foot of the person next to them, they say 「①sumimasen」 to apologize. In addition, when receiving a gift, people also say 「②sumimasen」 to express their thanks.

It is said that the word 「sumu」 in 「sumimasen」 originally came from the word 「澄む」, meaning clear or pure. 「澄む」 describes a state in which things such as water are clean and free of cloudiness. For this reason, it is also used when one’s heart feels peaceful and calm. When we accidentally do something wrong to another person, our heart is not at peace. Therefore, when apologizing, people say 「sumimasen」 because their 'heart is not clear and at peace.'

The reason people say 「sumimasen」 when receiving something from another person is also related to this. When someone treats us kindly, we ③ feel happy, but at the same time, we think that the person has gone to trouble for our sake, so our heart is no longer completely at peace. Thus, it is thought that 「sumimasen」 gradually came to be used when expressing thanks as well.

My mother looked just like a high school student.

I have a friend named Watanabe Emi. She is a friend I met at work about ten years ago. She is always cheerful, energetic, and carefree. Even when the department manager told her to submit a report, Emi would not submit it immediately. Whenever she caught a cold, she would take time off work right away. When I first came to Japan, I ate nothing but Chinese food. I went to Chinese restaurants and also cooked Chinese food for myself. Chinese dishes are generally stewed, grilled, or stir-fried, and vegetables are rarely eaten raw. However, I thought Japanese food consisted entirely of raw dishes such as sushi, sashimi, and salad, and that eating this way would make my body cold. As a result, I did not eat Japanese food even once.

Then one day, my friend Shoko said, "I found a really good Japanese restaurant. Let's go together!" Honestly, I did not want to go, but Shoko said she wanted to go with me, so I decided to join her. First, I ate sushi. The fish was raw. I had thought raw fish would smell fishy, but the sushi was not fishy at all and was delicious. After that, I ate various other dishes, such as tempura and grilled chicken skewers. I was very surprised because I had thought Japanese cuisine had no dishes cooked with fire. Everything was delicious. From then on, I came to enjoy Japanese food and began cooking it myself as well.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t23-p1.vietnamese:
Do you like 「traveling」? When we travel, we can visit many different places, see new and unusual things, and eat delicious food. In addition, visiting a place for the first time gives us a fresh feeling. Since there are many means of transportation, we can easily travel long distances.

For this reason, many people today probably think that 「traveling is enjoyable」. However, in the past, there were no trains or cars, so ordinary people had to travel on foot. They sometimes encountered danger along the way or became ill. In the past, traveling was not enjoyable; it was extremely difficult.

In classical Japanese literature, scenes often appear in which people leaving on journeys and those seeing them off say goodbye while crying. This was probably because once people set out on a long journey, they did not know whether they would survive and return home.

This is an essay written by Vikas.

It’s Difficult! Japanese Names

Andy Vikas

In the morning, I study Japanese at a Japanese-language school, and in the afternoon, I work at a Japanese company.

Before coming to Japan, I studied kanji hard. I thought studying kanji was interesting, and I thought I had memorized all the kanji used in everyday life. However, after coming to Japan, I realized that there were many people’s names I could not read. This was because sometimes their readings differed from those shown in kanji textbooks. For example, there is the name “Kondou-san.” The kanji 近 can be read as “chikai” and “kin.” Therefore, when I received a business card from Mr. Kondou, I accidentally said, “Are you Mr. Kintou?” However, his real name was “Kondou-san.” In addition, there are many names whose kanji I recognize but whose readings I do not know. Moreover, the same kanji can sometimes have different readings, as in “Otani-san” and “Oya-san” (both written 大谷), which surprised me greatly.

Even when I cannot read someone’s name, people kindly tell me how to read it, so I do not have any problems. However, I want to be able to correctly read many people’s names soon.

(Note) Business card: a card showing a person’s name, used for work and other purposes.

This is an essay written by Emma.

A Gift from Grandpa

Sanders Emma

When I was little, I used to receive birthday presents from my grandfather. After he was admitted to a hospital far away, I wrote down what I wanted as a gift on a piece of paper. My parents put the paper in an envelope, attached a stamp, and mailed it to him.

However, in reality, my parents were the ones who bought the gifts and sent them to me. I did not know that at all. I always thought that my grandfather was the one giving me the presents.

Before my sixth birthday, I wanted to send a letter to him by myself. I wrote 「To Grandpa at △△ Hospital」 on the envelope, wrote my own address, and put it in a mailbox. However, because I did not write the hospital's name correctly, the post office returned the letter to my home.

On my birthday, I received a present from my father and mother. At that time, they told me that they had actually bought the gifts and about my grandfather's illness. They said that his illness could no longer be cured.

The gift I received then was a watch with a princess design. I brought it with me to Japan, and it is now on my desk. It is my most precious possession because it was my last gift from my grandfather.

This is an essay written by Ryu.

White Does Not Cause Fatigue

Ryu Bun

I have played sports since I was a child. I used to think that was a good thing.

This happened when I had a part-time job transporting goods. The goods were not very heavy. However, by the time my work was almost over, I would be tired and barely able to move. That was because the goods gradually seemed to become heavier. In reality, they had not actually become heavier. Their weight remained the same, but they felt heavy to me.

I presented my idea about this to the director of the company where I worked part-time. I said that the color of the boxes should be changed to white. This is because white gives a lighter impression than black or brown. For example, sports shirts and socks are mostly white. They make people feel lighter and able to move more. The company’s boxes were originally brown. I told the director that white would make the work easier.

The director listened very attentively to my story. Then, one month later, white boxes were delivered. From that point on, the work became much easier. I learned this because I had played sports. It was not something I learned from studying books. I think that whether through sports or recreation, we can find useful ideas for our work.

What Matters

Achira Katokurundage

Late at night three days ago, I bought some food at a convenience store and returned home. As soon as I opened my bag after arriving home, I was startled. My wallet was gone. Although it was an inexpensive wallet, it contained many kinds of cards as well as my part-time wages. Losing any of those things would have caused serious trouble.

I immediately ran out of the house and searched for the wallet with my friends, but we could not find it.

The next day, I consulted my teachers at school and went to the police box near my home, but in the end, nothing came of it.

While I was crying in distress, I received a call from a teacher. Apparently, a man named Yamamoto had found the wallet near the convenience store. After seeing my school ID, he called my school. That evening, I arranged to meet Mr. Yamamoto in front of the convenience store.

Mr. Yamamoto looked like a very kind person. He handed me the wallet and said, 「Open it and check whether everything inside is still there.」 All the money and cards were exactly as they had been. I thanked him: 「Thank you so very much.」

When I returned home, looking at the wallet and remembering Mr. Yamamoto’s face filled me with a warm feeling. I thought that if I found someone’s lost belongings, I would also want to do the same thing.

This is an essay written by Marie.

My Grandmother

Marie Jimenez

My grandmother’s name is「Yu」. However, she is not my biological grandmother. Grandma Yu lives alone in the house next door. Exactly one year ago, on my way home from school, Grandma Yu spoke to me. I had had an argument with a friend at school and had thought that I no longer wanted to go to school. Grandma Yu listened gently to my story and said, “That must have been very hard for you,” and before long, I regained the desire to return to school. My late biological grandmother also always listened gently to me and cheered me up. That is why I have always considered Grandma Yu to be my grandmother too.

I heard that someone like Grandma Yu once had a difficult time as well. It was when her husband died. I heard that she had no desire to do anything and spent every day sitting and looking out at the garden. One day, however, she realized that the cherry blossoms in the garden were in full bloom. Cherry blossoms were her husband’s favorite flowers, and Grandma Yu apparently thought they were a message from him: “You cannot go on like this forever.” From then on, Grandma Yu (      ).

I heard that the character「優」in Grandma Yu’s name means gentle and kind. Neighbors often come to Grandma Yu’s house to chat. Everyone always leaves with a bright smile. I think it must be Grandma Yu’s kind heart that makes people feel this way.

（Note 1）旦那さん (husband): In this passage, it means Grandma Yu’s husband.

（Note 2）にこにこして (smiling): Smiling with a bright, gentle expression.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t267-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, I began learning to play the piano. Last year, when I turned 60 and retired, I had more free time. I had continuously studied piano since childhood, but in high school I quit because I became too busy with my studies. After I started working, I worked so much overtime that I no longer thought about the piano. However, about six months after retiring, I happened to find a flyer in the newspaper for a piano class for adults. Seeing it reminded me that I had once studied piano. That made me want to try playing again.

After returning to the piano following such a long break, I discovered a kind of enjoyment completely different from what I had experienced as a child. When I was young, I simply played so that I would not make mistakes, following exactly what was written in the score. I was very happy whenever I played correctly and well, and my teachers praised me as well. Now, however, rather than focusing on avoiding mistakes, my teachers teach me how to perform a piece. They discuss with me the images and feelings conveyed by the music, saying things like, “Try playing the opening gently,” or “From this section onward, the joy will gradually build.” As a result, I find it fascinating that I can turn my own emotional images into the sound of the piano.

Every October, there is a recital where the teachers and students present the results of their work. I would like to take part in this year’s recital. Although my playing is still clumsy, I will practice hard and (would like to convey my own impressions and images to everyone).

This is an essay written by an international student.

I came to Japan two years ago. I thought Japan was a very convenient and easy country to live in because it has so many convenience stores and supermarkets.

However, there is one unfortunate thing: there is a great deal of waste. When walking through the streets, you hardly see any litter and everything is clean, but living in Japan produces a great deal of garbage. For example, when I buy snacks, I find that each snack is individually wrapped in a plastic bag when I open the package. Every time I eat one snack, another piece of garbage is added. The other day, when I bought tomatoes at a supermarket, I found that they had been placed in a plastic container and wrapped in plastic film. When I returned home and cooked, both the plastic container and the plastic film became garbage. As a result, the garbage bin in my home quickly became filled with plastic waste.

It is true that this makes snacks and tomatoes look clean and is convenient for people who live alone. However, I do not think it is necessary to put each individual snack or tomato in a plastic bag or place it in a plastic container. If plastic bags and plastic wrapping were not used, (the amount of garbage would certainly decrease).

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t279-p1.vietnamese:
This is an essay written by an international student.

The Yamada Family and Me

Anna

Last week, I went to the Yamada family’s house. Their house is far from my apartment, so I had to take a train and a bus. Since it was my first time taking a train and a bus, I was very worried and thought, “What should I do if I take the wrong one?” When I told Yamada about it, Yamada asked their father to drive to my apartment and pick me up. Yamada’s father immediately agreed cheerfully: “Of course I can, dear.”

When I arrived at the Yamada family’s house, Yamada’s mother and younger sister, who is in high school, came out to greet me. I gave the family a souvenir I had bought in my country and said, “Let’s drink it together.” Everyone then looked a little awkward. The souvenir I had brought was wine. In my country, people often drink wine while eating together. However, Yamada’s parents cannot drink alcohol, and Yamada and the younger sister are not yet allowed to drink. I thought to myself, “Oh no.” I thought that if I bought a souvenir, I should have asked beforehand what kind of things the family liked. However, the Yamada family happily accepted it and said they were glad because it was a rare wine.

Then the whole family made and ate takoyaki together, played games, and talked a lot. It was an extremely enjoyable day.

Japanese people often nod and give verbal responses while listening to someone speak. Aizuchi means repeatedly saying things like “yeah, yeah,” “I see,” or “That’s right,” or nodding one’s head up and down. These responses convey the message, “I’m listening to your story,” and “Please go on.”

However, some cultures abroad believe that when listening to someone, it is better to look the other person in the eye and say nothing until they have finished speaking. When such a person talks with a Japanese person, the foreign speaker may find it noisy or annoying that the Japanese listener keeps saying things like “yeah, yeah” and “yes, yes.” Conversely, when Japanese people are speaking, they may feel uneasy or anxious because the foreign listener does not nod or give verbal responses.

When cultures differ, communication styles differ as well. I experienced the Japanese New Year for the first time.

On December 31, I first went with Mr. Nakayama to a supermarket near our home at 9:00 a.m. I did not buy anything, but I saw many people at the supermarket buying more food than usual. I heard that they were buying it to prepare special dishes eaten during the New Year. Apparently, there is a custom of preparing these special dishes before December 31 and eating them from January 1 through January 3. However, Mr. Nakayama said that these days some people eat at restaurants starting on January 1.

On January 1, I went to a shrine with my senior and some friends. What surprised me was the enormous number of people planning to visit the shrine, forming a long, continuous line. While I was standing outside the shrine, I suddenly could not find my wallet. I had heard that some people have their wallets stolen while waiting in front of shrines every year, so I thought mine had been stolen too. However, after searching carefully, I found it in my bag. At last, I entered the shrine and prayed, “May the new year be a good one.” At the shrine, my senior drew an omikuji fortune. Drawing an omikuji means receiving a piece of paper stating whether the year will be a good one. I heard that my senior’s fortune contained good predictions. Then, in the late afternoon, I returned home.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t297-p1.vietnamese:
You probably do not pay much attention to it normally, but are you sure you use chopsticks properly? You need to be especially careful when eating Japanese food with others in Japan. Japanese cuisine has many habits that should be avoided, collectively called “kiraibashi.”

For example, “neburi-bashi” means using your mouth to clean food stuck to your chopsticks; “mayoi-bashi” means moving your chopsticks from side to side while deciding what to eat; and “sashi-bashi” means spearing food with your chopsticks. There are also “yose-bashi,” pulling a plate toward yourself; “namida-bashi,” allowing liquid to run down your chopsticks; and “wataribashi,” placing your chopsticks across a plate or bowl. There are many other types as well.

Recently, it is not only children who do not know how to use chopsticks; many people do not even know how to hold them correctly. One reason is that they eat more Western food and fast food. Another is that they have fewer opportunities to eat with their parents, and their parents did not teach them properly. If a foreigner asks us how to hold chopsticks and we cannot explain it, we Japanese feel embarrassed.

In the evening, I review what I studied that day and sometimes prepare for the next day’s lessons. Then I take a bath and go to sleep immediately afterward.

Last winter, I traveled to Hokkaido with my friend Cheon from South Korea, who was studying at the same Japanese-language school. While I was in Taiwan, I had taught myself Japanese by reading books, so I was especially good at writing and reading kanji, but my listening and speaking skills were still poor. One thing that worried me was that if we flew, the flight might not operate or might be delayed on days when Hokkaido had heavy snow. Since it does not snow in my country, I was also very excited about seeing snow. Above all, what I was looking forward to most was seeing the Snow Festival.

On the evening we arrived in Sapporo, we went to see the Snow Festival that we had been eagerly anticipating. Many “snow sculptures,” including buildings, animals, celebrities from the previous year, and cartoon characters, had been made from snow and arranged in long rows. The visitors were not only Japanese; there were also many people from other countries. After viewing the snow sculptures, we ate Sapporo ramen, which was another thing I had been looking forward to. Then we went to see the famous clock tower, headed toward Otaru, and bathed in a hot spring. Although it was a short trip, it became a wonderfully enjoyable vacation.

Tada Akiko and Sakaki Fuyumi's marriage criteria
Akiko wants her husband to have their own home and live separately from his parents. Fuyumi wants to live with her in-laws and does not want to marry a younger man.
The living circumstances of Higashiyama Norio and Saijou Hideyoshi.
Norio lives with his mother in Tokyo and does not have a car. Hideyoshi lives alone in Tokyo and does not have a car.
The living circumstances of Minami Haruto and Kitajima Ichirou
Haruto lives in Chiba, has a car, and has parents in Shizuoka, making him suitable for Kana. Ichirou lives in Yokohama, has a small car, and wants to live with his parents.

A. Women’s Marriage Preferences

Miyako Harue (36)
After getting married, I want to live at his family home and learn how to cook while having his mother teach me many things. On days off, I want to go somewhere together in his car. Since I want to get married soon, age does not matter to me if he is a good person.

Watanabe Kana (32)
After getting married, I want to live alone with him. I do not think my personality is very good, so if he were younger than me or if we lived with his parents, we might argue. On days off, I also want to go somewhere together by car.

Tada Akiko (35)

Sakaki Fuyumi (33)

Higashiyama Norio (31)

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t35-p1.vietnamese:
When was the moment you realized that you had become an adult?

My older sister answered that it was when her relationship with our parents changed. In the past, whenever our parents reminded her not to do something or told her that she had to do something, she would become irritated and complain, saying things like “How annoying” and “I know.” However, after she began living independently, she said that she came to understand the feelings of our parents, who had always scolded and taught her. Since then, she said, her relationship with them has improved.

Not long ago, I took a taxi by myself. I was in danger of being late for an appointment because of work. It was the first time I had ever taken a taxi alone. Then I thought, “Ah, I guess I’ve become an adult too.” Until then, I had avoided taxis because they cost more than trains, but another reason was that I could not decide on my own whether I should take one. Making decisions by yourself is not at all simple.

When I asked other people, I received many different answers, such as when they graduated from high school or university, or when they first entered a restaurant alone. Perhaps people gradually become adults by accumulating various experiences, such as leaving their family and friends to enter a new world or becoming able to do something on their own.

To everyone using the community center's rooms

● Please do not eat or drink in the rooms.

● The air conditioner's cooling mode may be used from June through September, and its heating mode from November through March. If you wish to use it outside these periods, please inform the reception desk.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t41-p1.vietnamese:
Because exercise is good for the body, more and more people are trying to walk instead of taking elevators or buses. The reason is that people are busy and do not have time to exercise. They do not need to go to a sports club, and since walking is simple even for someone like me who does not particularly enjoy exercise, I think it is a good idea.

Erika, who works at the same company as I do, also walks very often. I heard that she did not like exercise at first, but walking became enjoyable, so she started jogging too. Erika invited me, saying, «Jogging in the park has been so refreshing lately. Would you like to come and try it sometime?», so when I went to that park on Sunday, I was extremely surprised to see so many people jogging. Erika looked very happy to have someone to run with.

I heard that Erika will participate in a marathon for the first time next month. She said that she used to be able to run only very slowly, but now she can run a little faster, so she wants to be able to run 10 km in one hour.

I used to think that people who liked exercise from childhood were the ones who started jogging as adults, but apparently that is not the case. From now on, I am planning to start by walking too.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t42-p1.vietnamese:
Regarding the Use of City A Library

○ People who may use it

People who live in City A; people who work in City A; people who attend schools in City A; and people who live in City B, City C, or City D.

○ Borrowing materials

When borrowing materials for the first time, please make a library card at the library reception desk.

Each person may borrow a total of up to 10 books and magazines. Up to 3 CDs may be borrowed for a period of 2 weeks.

＊ People aged 60 or older may borrow up to 5 CDs.

＊ People from outside City A may not borrow CDs.

＊ DVDs cannot be borrowed.

○ Returning materials

Please return materials at the reception desk. When the library is closed, please return them to the book-return box at the entrance.

＊ CDs must be returned at the reception desk.

○ When you have not finished reading a book by its due date

Before the due date, please notify the reception desk or contact us by phone. You may borrow the book for an additional 2 weeks.

＊ If another person has already reserved the book, you may borrow it only until the original due date.

＊ CDs may be borrowed only until the original due date.

Put groceries in the refrigerator as soon as you get home, and eat food immediately after cooking it. Try not to eat anything that has been left out too long or has spoiled. In addition, washing your hands is very important. Be sure to wash your hands when you return home from outside. Of course, wash them before cooking as well. Rinsing with water alone is not enough. ◇◇◇ Would you like to volunteer as a helper at an international conference? ◇◇◇

In May, an international conference for visually impaired people will be held in Tokyo. At the conference, visually impaired people from around the world will discuss a variety of topics together.

We are looking for 30 people to assist visually impaired visitors from overseas who come to Japan to attend the conference. Would you like to participate in activities such as meeting them at the airport or showing them around Tokyo?

Volunteer requirements are……

1. Both Japanese and non-Japanese people may apply.

2. Japanese applicants must speak a foreign language, while non-Japanese applicants must know Japanese. For Japanese, applicants need to have passed N4 or a higher level. Those who have never taken the N4 will take a simple test of conversation and kanji.

3. The conference will last three days. We ask that applicants be able to participate for at least two days.

One month before the conference begins, we will hold three training sessions for volunteers. Please be sure to attend all of them. Since this is not paid part-time work, we cannot provide compensation, but all transportation costs, such as trains, buses, and taxis, incurred while accompanying visually impaired people will be fully covered.

Do you know the term 「席次」 (seating order)? It means which seat is the best, and which seats are second-best, third-best, and so on.

When entering a room, we are sometimes unsure where each person should sit. Older people, such as teachers and senior colleagues, as well as guests, should be seated farther from the entrance. Remember that the seat farthest from the entrance is the guest seat. Conversely, people from the household—not guests—or younger people should sit near the entrance. Being near the entrance is more convenient when serving guests tea, cakes, or other refreshments.

There are also rules governing seating order in taxis and elevators. In a taxi, the seat next to the driver has the lowest rank. In an elevator, the position near the floor buttons or the 「Open / Close」 door buttons has a low rank. Whether traveling by taxi or elevator, let teachers, senior colleagues, and guests enter first and leave first. The seat next to the taxi driver or the position in front of the elevator buttons has a meaning similar to that of the position near a room’s entrance.

Although the idea that guests should sit far from the entrance is useful, the guest’s feelings and wishes are actually the most important consideration. If someone at a restaurant says they would like to enjoy the meal while looking at the beautiful garden, let them sit where they can see outside well, even if that seat is near the entrance.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t5-p1.vietnamese:
This summer, I stayed with my family at a hotel deep in the mountains.

It took more than two hours by bus to get from the train station to the bus stop near the hotel. From the bus stop to the hotel, we walked for nearly 30 minutes along a narrow path. The hotel was small and old, but the inside was very clean and beautiful. However, it did not even have a television. Moreover, there was neither a refrigerator nor air conditioning. Although the hotel lacked conveniences, we were able to experience many interesting things in the mountains and around the lake.

After putting our luggage in the room and opening the window, a cool breeze from the lake rushed in. After resting for a while, we went outside for a walk because it was still light. The air was fresh and pleasant, and the scenery was extremely beautiful. At night, the stars sparkled brilliantly. Throughout our stay at the hotel, everyone went for a walk and then swam in the lake every day. We caught insects and then took afternoon naps.

We stayed at the hotel for 1 week. Saying to one another, “This is fun, isn't it? It’s nice to live like this once in a while,” we returned home together.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t50-p1.vietnamese:
When talking on the telephone, why do people say "もしもし" (moshi moshi, “hello”)? It is said that this expression originated as an abbreviated form of "もうしあげます、もうしあげます" (“I would like to speak”), meaning “I am going to speak now,” when telephones were first introduced.

However, recently, more and more people have been saying that one should not use "もしもし". Let us consider what happens when calling a company. Suppose the person answering says, “Yes, hello.” The caller then does not know which company they have reached and may feel uneasy. As a result, they have to ask again, “Hello, is this OO Trading Company?” What if, instead of saying “hello” at the beginning, the person answering said, “Yes, OO Trading Company speaking”? The caller could immediately give their name—“This is △△”—and get down to business. It is said that some companies even have new employees practice not saying "もしもし" when they start working.

One might want to say, “From today on, please do not say it when it is unnecessary,” but this expression, which was born together with the telephone, also carries meanings such as “Can you hear me?” and “I am listening.” Would it not still be acceptable when speaking with someone who can recognize the other person just by their voice, or when calling an elderly person?

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t60-p1.vietnamese:
About 30 years ago in Japan, it was normal for men to work for a company until the age of 60. It was also normal for women to leave their jobs after getting married or having children. Even if the wife did not work, the entire family could live comfortably as long as they had the income the husband received from his company.

I think it was a wonderful period when families could live securely without worrying about money. Compared with today, when Japan's economy has deteriorated, income from work has decreased, and people have lost their jobs, I think that period was much better.

However, that period seems to have been a terrible one for women who enjoyed their jobs and wanted to work like men.

Today, because the income a husband receives from work is no longer enough to support a family, women continue working even after getting married. As a result, the opposite way of thinking from the past has begun to spread. Young women have started to think that they want to stay at home after getting married, raise their children, and try to do other things besides working, while young men have begun to think that they will help with housework and therefore want women to continue working throughout their lives.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t66-p1.vietnamese:
When our eyesight deteriorates and it becomes difficult to see things, we use eyeglasses or contact lenses. By doing so, we can see things that were difficult to see before. Both eyeglasses and contact lenses are essential items for people with poor eyesight.

However, eyeglasses and contact lenses are ① not the same.

First, because eyeglasses are worn on the face, other people can immediately tell that you are wearing them. Contact lenses, on the other hand, are placed inside the eyes, so even if you wear them, other people <u>② cannot tell</u>.

Also, eyeglasses may slip or fall off during exercise, making it difficult to move, whereas contact lenses rarely have <u>③ this happen</u>, no matter how much you move, so they are convenient for exercise. However, they can also be dangerous. If a ball hits an eye wearing a contact lens, the eye may be injured.

Considering the advantages of both, I use contact lenses when playing sports and try to wear eyeglasses when studying or reading.

This is a guide to garbage disposal.

In this ward, garbage collection days differ depending on the address where you live.

For burnable garbage, residents of Kitamachi and Higashimachi should put it out on Tuesdays, while residents of Minamimachi and Nishimachi should put it out on Mondays and Wednesdays. For non-burnable garbage, residents of Kitamachi and Higashimachi should put it out on the first and third Saturdays of the month, while residents of Minamimachi and Nishimachi should put it out on the second and fourth Saturdays. Many people may think that when a major earthquake occurs, the first priority should be to put out fires. However, a government investigation found that many people were burned or injured in falls because they hurried to extinguish fires. During a major earthquake, glass and other objects may also fall and break. Rather than putting out fires, we should first prioritize avoiding injury, such as protecting our heads. Get under a table, or if there is no table nearby, sit where you are and protect your head. Large bookcases may topple over, so be careful not to go near them.

(Note 1) Investigation: asking many people for their opinions in order to learn about or survey something.

(Note 2) Burn: an injury caused by touching something hot or being splashed with boiling water.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t74-p1.vietnamese:
The day when chocolate sells best in Japan is February 14, Valentine's Day. This is because in Japan there is a custom of women giving chocolate to men on Valentine's Day. As Valentine's Day approaches, chocolate booths appear in supermarkets and department stores, displaying chocolates in cute colors and shapes.

This custom is said to have begun when a chocolate company launched a promotional campaign with the slogan 'Give chocolate on Valentine's Day' in the latter half of the 1950s. Then, around 1970, influenced by confectionery companies' advertisements, the day began to be regarded as 'the day when women give chocolate to the man they like.' In addition, at companies, a custom gradually emerged in which female employees gave 'Giri-choco (courtesy chocolate)' to male colleagues they worked with, even when they did not have any particular romantic feelings for them. Recently, however, an increasing number of women have stopped giving 'Giri-choco' for reasons such as the expense, the difficulty of deciding whom to give it to and whom not to, or simply wanting to give chocolate only to someone they genuinely like.

（Note 1）Chocolate: a type of sweet confectionery

（Note 2）Campaign: various activities intended to sell a product...

（Note 3）Influence: the effect of something that is manifested in other things as well

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t75-p1.vietnamese:
This is a story told by a teacher at a cram school.

When children bring home tests with low scores, most parents become angry and say things like「Study more」or ask suspiciously,「Are you really studying?」Some even insult their children, saying「You’re so stupid」. However, according to the teacher, this is the one thing that absolutely must not be said.

「A child who is spoken to that way will gradually start thinking,『I’m stupid, so there’s no point in studying』」.

The teacher said that he first asks a child who received a low score:「How did you feel at that moment?」The child then answers with things like「I’m so disappointed」or「Actually, I should have been able to do better」. Next, when the teacher asks,「Then how would you like to feel next time?」, the child often gives a positive answer such as「I want to get a good score and feel happy」. The teacher then lets the child think for themselves about the cause of the low score and how to address it in order to achieve that sense of happiness. As a result, children reportedly gradually begin studying proactively on their own, even when they are alone.

(Note 1) じゅく (cram school): A place that provides instruction outside the regular school system.

(Note 2) うたがう (to doubt): To think that the other person may be lying.

(Note 3) 前むき (positive): Being proactive and willing to do something.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t76-p1.vietnamese: What is a 「teacher」 whom we can trust like? One possible answer is 「someone who knows everything」. Indeed, a teacher who can immediately answer anything you ask may seem trustworthy. Many people probably think that it is shameful for a teacher not to know something. However, in today's society, technology is constantly advancing and new things keep appearing one after another. New ways of thinking are also continually emerging, and this process is much faster than it used to be. Of course, old knowledge can still be useful at times. But no matter how much old knowledge a teacher possesses, I cannot trust a teacher who is unwilling to learn new things. In contrast, the teacher I can trust is someone who understands that it is natural to have 「things one does not understand」 and that they themselves still have much to learn. I think such a teacher would never mock a student for not knowing something by saying, 「You don't even know that?」 If they do not know something, they do not pretend to know it; instead, they look it up and investigate it carefully. I would like to study under a teacher like that.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t77-p1.vietnamese:
When a child or someone you love is crying intensely, what is the best way to make them stop? Usually, people encourage or comfort them, right? Some people may tell a funny story in an attempt to make them forget why they are crying. Or, if the other person is a child, some mothers may scold them and tell them to stop crying. However, all of these approaches have the opposite effect. The other person feels that no one understands why they are crying, and as a result, they cry even more intensely.

In fact, it is said that the most effective method is to cry even louder than the other person. This method may seem as though it would solve nothing, but what a crying person wants most is for the other person to share their feelings. This is called「empathy」. For someone who is crying or angry, that is much more meaningful than receiving the correct answer. If someone is crying, try crying with them; if someone is laughing, try laughing with them.

default.p.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t78-p1.vietnamese:
A Bus Tour

On Sunday, I went on a bus tour with my friend Satoshi. Recently, there have been many different kinds of bus tours. In addition to tours that visit famous destinations, there are tours for enjoying delicious fruit, shopping at discount stores, and so on. The tour we took was called a mystery tour. Before setting out, we did not know where we were going.

I arranged to meet Satoshi in front of the bus we were going to take, but when I left the station and went to the bus departure area, there were many similar buses, so I did not know which one was ours. While I was confused, I received a call on my mobile phone, and he told me that he was in front of the bus parked farthest from the station.

After about two hours on the bus, it entered a narrow road. As the bus climbed higher, the road became narrower and narrower, which made my heart jump. When we reached the parking lot and got off the bus, we climbed a steep staircase from there. A river was flowing below us. Since it had rained, the water level was high and the current was fast, so I felt frightened. When we reached the very top of the stairs, I heard a very loud sound. It was a waterfall. I could see water falling from a great height after splitting into two streams.

Nishi City Library borrowing regulations

1. Dictionaries and the latest newspapers and magazines must be read inside the library.

(Note 2) Materials: Here, books, CDs, cassette tapes, records, DVDs, and similar items held by the library

It follows a noun directly to indicate the subject or topic that the writer is about to explain or describe in detail. With the correct answer, the complete title is「北市町工場見学について」, meaning "About the factory tour in Kitashi Town." To avoid confusion in N4 reading passages, remember that「～によると」cites a source ('according to...'),「～によって」indicates a cause, agent, or variation ('depending on...'), while announcements about an event or plan use「N + について」.

Here, the fact that chocolate sells well in February is a market phenomenon caused by Valentine’s Day, so「ため」is correct both grammatically and in nuance. Remember the distinction:「おかげで」(thanks to) implies gratitude for a positive result,「せいで」(because of) expresses blame for a negative result, while「ため」simply states a causal relationship. It commonly combines with nouns referring to events, conferences, or ceremonies in the pattern 「[event] が 行われる」 to indicate that something is held or takes place naturally and objectively. default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t108-q1.explanatio: Based on the sentence in the passage: 「少し前まで星空（　Ａ　）ないようなテカポ村には旅行者はほとんど来なかった。」, the predicate after the blank is in the negative form 「ない」, which requires the particle 「しか」 to create the structure 「N + しか + V-ない」, meaning “only N; nothing other than N.” This grammar pattern emphasizes scarcity or limitation from the speaker’s subjective perspective, which fits the context of Tekapo at that time: a quiet village with little to attract visitors besides its starry sky. The completed sentence can be translated as: “Until fairly recently, hardly any tourists visited Tekapo, a village that seemed to have nothing but a starry sky.” An important N4 test-taking tip is that 「だけ」 is used with an affirmative predicate to express simple limitation, whereas 「しか」 must be accompanied by a negative predicate (ない/ません) to express “only.”

Since the passage uses Shibuya Crossing as the central reference point and people are coming from various places toward it, 集まってくる (come together here) is the correct choice. To avoid confusing it with (b) 集まっていく, remember: use 〜てくる for movement toward the reference point and 〜ていく for movement away from it.

The pattern 「〜ことにした」 expresses a subjective, intentional decision. Here, it describes a decision made by the police in the past to address concerns about traffic accidents.
default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t110-q2.explanatio: The preceding sentence is「だから警察はいつも事故が起きないかと心配していた」("Therefore, the police were always worried that an accident might occur"). The next sentence therefore needs a structure expressing a measure or decision that the police proactively took:「それで2016年の大晦日にはスクランブル交差点に車を通さないことにした。」In JLPT N4 grammar,「V-る / V-ない + ことにする」(past: ことにした) expresses a subjective decision made with clear intention by an individual or organization to do or not do something. The complete sentence means: "For that reason, on New Year’s Eve in 2016, the police decided not to let cars pass through the Shibuya Scramble Crossing." To avoid confusion, distinguish「〜ことにする」(a subjective decision made by the subject) from「〜ことになる」(an outcome determined objectively by circumstances or external rules). Also,「〜ことがある」(something occasionally happens) and「〜ことだ」(advice about what one should do) cannot report a specific decision made at a definite past time,「2016年の大晦日には」.

default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t117-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 笑えば笑うほど
Filling in the structure「〜ば〜ほど」(the more... the more...) completes the meaning: the more one laughs, the more cheerful and healthy one seems to live.
default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t117-q2.explanatio: The key N4 grammar pattern 「V-えば + V-る + ほど」 means “the more..., the more...,” expressing a corresponding change in the second clause as the degree of the action or state in the first clause increases. In the sentence 「（　B　）元気で楽しい生活ができるようだ。」, the author is summarizing the benefits of smiling after explaining that laughter strengthens the immune system and reduces stress. Therefore, the correct form of 笑う (to laugh) is the conditional form 「笑えば」 followed by the dictionary form and 「ほど」: 「笑えば笑うほど」. The complete sentence means: “The more we laugh, the more likely we are to live a cheerful and healthy life.” Remember the fixed pattern 「〜ば〜ほど」; do not replace it with the conditional 「〜と」 or combine it with the degree expression 「ぐらい」.

Choice (b) uses the N4 pattern 「A は B ほど + V-ない」, in which A is marked by は, B is the comparison standard with ほど, and the predicate is negative to express that A is less than B. Beware of the mathematical trap in choice (c): 60% is not twice (2倍) 40%. The numerical relationship 40% < 60% corresponds to the comparison pattern 「〜ほど〜ない」.

default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t118-q1.explanatio: Based on the sentence in the passage: 「技能実習生は技術を学ぶために来たのに彼らは安いお金で（　A　）。」 The key grammar point is the causative-passive form combined with the progressive ending (使役受身形 + ている). The Group 1 verb 働く changes to 働かせられる ➔ 働かせられている, expressing that the subject is being forced by someone to do something against their wishes. The complete translation is: “Although the technical trainees came to learn skills, they are being made to work for very low wages.” The important distinction is to identify the subject’s role: 「彼らは」 are the people being forced to work, not the managers, so the active causative in choice (a) cannot be used. Japanese uses the causative-passive (“be made to work”) rather than the simple passive when expressing coercion.

default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t118-q2.verdict:

default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t118-q2.explanatio: The N4 pattern 「V-ます (ます-stem) + にくい」 expresses that something is difficult to do, whether because of circumstances or subjective experience. It functions as an i-adjective and directly modifies 「国」 in 「働きにくい国」 (“a country where it is difficult to work”). Paragraph 1 states 「今の日本は働きやすい社会ではないのだ。」 (“Japan today is not a society that is easy to work in”) because its employment system and conditions still have many limitations. Therefore, the blank requires the corresponding negative expression: 「日本が今のように（ 働きにくい ）国のままだったら、外国人は日本を選ばないだろう。」 This means: “If Japan continues to be a country where it is difficult to work, foreigners probably will not choose Japan.” Do not choose (a), 「働きやすい」, because the consequence 「選ばない」 (“will not choose”) requires a negative context. Also, 「V-すぎる」 in (c) expresses an excessive action or degree, not the nature of a country’s working environment.
default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t118-q2.why.0: ✗ (a) 「働きやすい」 (“easy to work in”) has a positive meaning, which is completely opposite to the harsh working conditions analyzed in the passage.

It directly contrasts with 「働きたくても働けない」, which combines the desire form V-たい with the negative potential form V-えない: 'even though they want to work, they cannot.' Thus, a society that is 「働きやすい」is one that resolves these problems and makes it possible for everyone who wants to work to do so (働きたい人が働ける). default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t119-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) らしい
The structure 「〜かららしい」 presents an inference or reported information based on the objective basis or reason stated in the preceding clause. 「らしい」 can follow the cause particle 「から」 directly without any change.
default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t119-q1.explanatio: Grammatically, 「らしい」 can follow the causal particle 「から」 directly to form 「〜かららしい」, presenting an inference or reported information supported by objective evidence. The original sentence containing the blank is: 「こんなに多いのは①日本であまり戦争が起きなかったから、②企業が本業(注2)を大切にしてきたから、③企業に長期の視点(注3)があったから（ A ）。」 It begins with 「こんなに多いのは〜」 and gives the reasons for the statistical figures in the preceding sentence. The complete sentence means: "The reason there seem to be so many long-established companies is apparently that: ① wars rarely occurred in Japan, ② companies have valued their core businesses, and ③ companies have had a long-term perspective." For a quick distinction, remember that 「そうだ」 for hearsay requires 「〜からだそうだ」, and 「ようだ」 requires 「〜からのようだ」. Only 「らしい」 can follow 「から」 directly in this sentence.

default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t119-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) The hearsay form 「そうだ」 does not combine directly with 「から」 alone. If reporting the reason, the form must be 「〜からだそうだ」.
default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t119-q1.why.2: ✓ (c) 「らしい」 can combine directly with a particle indicating cause to form 「〜かららしい」, expressing an inference or reported information based on objective grounds.

default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t119-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) さ
The suffix 「さ」combines with the stem of the na-adjective 「大切」to form the noun 「大切さ」, meaning “importance.” It fits grammatically and semantically with 「～がわかる」.
default.q.luyenthi_dochieu_n4-t119-q2.explanatio: The relevant sentence is: 「特にバブル期に本業ではなく土地や建物を売ったり買ったりした多くの会社がその後会社を止めたり会社が苦しくなったことを考えると本業の大切さがわかる。」 This means: "In particular, when we consider how many companies during the bubble period bought and sold land and buildings instead of focusing on their core business, only to go bankrupt or fall into difficulty afterward, we can understand the importance of a core business." The key N4 grammar point is the nominalizing suffix 「〜さ」. It is formed by taking the stem of an i-adjective (removing い) or the stem of a na-adjective (removing な) and adding さ, creating a noun that expresses an objective degree or quality. Here, 「大切（な）」 becomes 「大切さ」, meaning importance.
